content: Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of paliperidone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both ketoconazole and paliperidone prolong the QTc interval, necessitating therapy modification and close monitoring. Ketoconazole increases panobinostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The starting dose of panobinostat should be reduced to 10 mg when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of parecoxib by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of paricalcitol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of paromomycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole and paroxetine both prolong the QTc interval, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Ketoconazole and pazopanib both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of perampanel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of phenytoin by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of pimozide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of pioglitazone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the toxicity of pitavastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, and monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), which is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase unconjugated MMAE exposure and polatuzumab toxicities. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of posaconazole by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both ketoconazole and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Ketoconazole increases the toxicity of pravastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of praziquantel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of prednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of prednisone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of progesterone intravaginal gel, micronized progesterone, and natural progesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of propafenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of quetiapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The quetiapine dose should be reduced to one-sixth of the original dose when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of quizartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Adjust quizartinib dosage when co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of rabeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifabutin decreases ketoconazole levels by increasing its metabolism through CYP3A4 induction. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin decreases ketoconazole levels by increasing its metabolism through CYP3A4 induction. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases rifaximin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. No rilpivirine dose adjustment is required, but clinical monitoring for breakthrough fungal infections is recommended when azole antifungals are co-administered. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of riociguat by decreasing its metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor for signs of hypotension and reduce the dose if needed. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ripretinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of risperidone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both ketoconazole and risperidone prolong the QTc interval, necessitating therapy modification and close monitoring. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels of roflumilast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both ketoconazole and romidepsin prolong the QTc interval, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of sacubitril/valsartan through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase valsartan systemic exposure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Adjust saxagliptin dosage to 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ketoconazole increases the levels of seladelpar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers and are co-administered moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of selexipag through mechanisms involving ABCG2 (BCRP) inhibition. Monitor for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects when co-administered with ABCG2 (BCRP) inhibitors. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Sodium bicarbonate decreases ketoconazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Caution and monitoring are advised. Sodium citrate/citric acid decreases ketoconazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Caution and monitoring are advised. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases ketoconazole toxicity through mechanisms involving fluid and electrolyte abnormalities, which may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Caution and monitoring are advised. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate decreases ketoconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer drugs at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. St. John’s Wort decreases ketoconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of streptomycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Sucralfate decreases ketoconazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of sufentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Consider dosage reduction of sufentanil until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals. If a CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing sufentanil dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. Ketoconazole and sulfamethoxazole both prolong the QTc interval, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus ointment by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Talazoparib is a P-glycoprotein substrate; co-administration with P-glycoprotein inhibitors may increase talazoparib systemic exposure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inhibition decreases the metabolism of tamoxifen to N-desmethyl tamoxifen, an active metabolite with similar biologic activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels of tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tasimelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole and telavancin both prolong the QTc interval, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of teniposide by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism but decreases its levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen when co-administered with a strong CYP3A inhibitor. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The ketoconazole dose should not exceed 200 mg/day when used concurrently. Ketoconazole increases the levels of tisotumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Its active metabolite (MMAE) is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase unconjugated MMAE systemic exposure and the risk of adverse effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tobramycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised.
